note: WAEC English round 7 (R43 top-up): synonyms abortive, brittle, concise, eradicate, feasible, grievous, immense, perilous, vivid; antonyms weary, mediocre, amicable, lengthy; idioms take after, keep body and soul together, on the spur of the moment, red-letter day, rainy day, up in arms; would rather, had better, put off, run into; orals silent s in island, noun stress in record. Scanned against the whole English pool (WAEC and NECO stems).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: All their attempts to repair the broken bridge proved ABORTIVE. ABORTIVE means
questions.explanation: Nothing came of the effort.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Old rubber bands become BRITTLE and snap easily. BRITTLE means
questions.explanation: Brittle things shatter at a touch.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The examiner asked for a CONCISE summary of the passage. CONCISE means
questions.explanation: Few words, all of them working.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The new health campaign aims to ERADICATE malaria from the region. ERADICATE means
questions.explanation: Not one case is to be left standing.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The committee judged the plan FEASIBLE within the budget. FEASIBLE means
questions.explanation: It can actually be carried out in practice.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The flood caused GRIEVOUS damage to the farms. GRIEVOUS means
questions.explanation: The loss cut deep into the farmers' season.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The stadium was filled with an IMMENSE crowd. IMMENSE means
questions.explanation: An immense sea of heads stretched to the gates.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The road through the forest is PERILOUS at night. PERILOUS means
questions.explanation: Travellers risk their lives on it.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The witness gave a VIVID account of the accident. VIVID means
questions.explanation: The hearer could almost see it happen.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: After trekking for six hours under the sun, the farmers were WEARY. A word opposite in meaning to WEARY is
questions.explanation: The weary have no strength left at all.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Critics called the team's performance MEDIOCRE. A word opposite in meaning to MEDIOCRE is
questions.explanation: Mediocre is neither poor nor praiseworthy.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: After months of quarrelling, the two chiefs finally reached an AMICABLE agreement. A word opposite in meaning to AMICABLE is
questions.explanation: Amicable talks are friendly talks.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The chairman's opening remarks were LENGTHY. A word opposite in meaning to LENGTHY is
questions.explanation: The lengthy speech ran on and on.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Everyone says Chidi TAKES AFTER his father. This means Chidi
questions.explanation: The likeness shows in face and manner.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: With his tiny salary, the watchman could barely KEEP BODY AND SOUL TOGETHER. This means he could barely
questions.explanation: Life itself was hard to sustain.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The family left the village ON THE SPUR OF THE MOMENT. This means they left
questions.explanation: The impulse alone moved them.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The day she won the scholarship was a RED-LETTER DAY for Ada. This means it was
questions.explanation: Red ink marks the days worth remembering.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The trader saves part of her profit every week FOR A RAINY DAY. This means she saves for
questions.explanation: The rainy day is the hard day that comes.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The villagers were UP IN ARMS over the new tax. This means they were
questions.explanation: Their anger stood up and shouted.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: I would rather ___ at home than go out in this rain.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' takes the bare infinitive.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: You have been coughing for a week; you ___ see a doctor without delay.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' gives strong advice.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The council has decided to ___ the ceremony until the rains are over.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb means to postpone.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: At the market I ___ an old classmate I had not seen for ten years.
questions.explanation: The meeting was quite by chance.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word 'island' contains a letter that is written but never pronounced. That letter is
questions.explanation: The s lies silent inside the word.

questions.q: When 'record' is used as a noun, as in 'a record of sales', the strong stress falls on its
questions.explanation: The verb reCORD becomes the noun RECord.
